title: ExecutionRequest v1
description: An intent submitted by IVE (or any other request-originating component) describing what it would like AEF to consider executing. This object grants NO authority by itself -- see prohibited_fields.ts. Every object level below sets additionalProperties=false except `parameters`, which is intentionally open (domain-specific) but is additionally scanned at runtime by the recursive prohibited-field check, since JSON Schema alone cannot express 'reject this field name at any nesting depth'.

contract_version.description: Must be exactly '1.0' for this schema version. Missing or mismatched -> reject, never assume a default (Section 18).

request_id.description: UUID v4. Uniquely identifies THIS request. Used for execution-replay defense -- a request with a previously-seen request_id must never be executed twice, distinct from idempotency_key (see docs).

correlation_id.description: Optional. Links multiple requests in the same reasoning/execution flow for tracing. Never used for authorization.

requested_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when this request was constructed.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. A request seen after this time must be rejected regardless of any other field (Section 15/9). Required unconditionally -- there is no such thing as a non-expiring ExecutionRequest in v1.

intent.description: Short, human/machine-readable description of what is being requested. Advisory/descriptive only -- never parsed for authorization decisions.

domain.description: Routing/classification only (Section 14). This value grants no permission by itself; each domain adapter applies its own policy.

action.description: Dot-namespaced action identifier, e.g. 'core.generate_strategy' or 'quant.controlled_live.submit_order'. Must be namespaced under a value consistent with `domain`.

resource.description: Optional. What the action targets, if anything (e.g. a project, a campaign). Descriptive only.

parameters.description: Domain/action-specific data. Intentionally NOT additionalProperties=false at the schema level (extensible per action), but is recursively scanned for PROHIBITED_AUTHORITY_FIELDS at runtime by validators.ts -- schema permissiveness here is not a security boundary, the scanner is.

constraints.description: Optional, ADVISORY ONLY. E.g. a caller-suggested budget ceiling. Never authoritative -- a future AEF Cost Guard makes the real determination independently.

quant_execution_tier.description: Required when domain='quant' (enforced in validators.ts, not expressible in pure JSON Schema without knowing the action taxonomy). Must exactly match the tier named in the second dot-segment of `action` whenever that segment is itself one of these five tier names (e.g. action='quant.controlled_live.submit_order' requires quant_execution_tier='controlled_live') -- this field is intentionally redundant with the action's own namespace, not an independent, freely-settable classifier, because a caller could otherwise under-declare risk (Codex adversarial review, Finding F-07: a request naming a 'controlled_live' action could previously claim tier='research' and skip the human-gate requirement below). controlled_live/expanded_live additionally require a non-null human_gate_ref pointing to an AUTHORIZED HumanGateRecord (Section 14/16).

context_ref.description: Optional reference to reasoning/context stored elsewhere (never embedded raw reasoning text here) -- keeps requests small and prevents requests from being used to smuggle authority-shaped free text into an unvalidated blob.

idempotency_key.description: Optional but strongly recommended for consequential actions. Distinct from request_id: a legitimate client retry (e.g. after a timeout) gets a NEW request_id but the SAME idempotency_key, so a future AEF can recognize 'same business operation, don't double-execute' without conflating it with 'exact same request replayed maliciously' (that's request_id's job) or 'this delegation nonce was reused' (that's DelegationEnvelope's job). See docs on the three distinct replay/idempotency concepts.

delegation_ref.description: Reference (ID) to a DelegationEnvelope that must independently exist and validate -- the envelope itself is never embedded in the request, so the request cannot act as its own proof of delegation.

human_gate_ref.description: Reference (ID) to a HumanGateRecord. Only meaningful for actions requiring human approval (e.g. quant_execution_tier=controlled_live). The request NEVER carries the approval decision itself -- only a pointer the authorizing layer independently resolves.

metadata.description: Optional, free-form STRING-only annotations. Explicitly documented and enforced (validators.ts) as NEVER consulted for authorization -- purely descriptive/telemetry. Still scanned for prohibited field names as defense-in-depth.

id.description: Claimed identity. NEVER trusted on its own -- see auth_ref.

auth_ref.description: Reference to a verifiable authentication assertion that an INDEPENDENT component (not the request's own author) must resolve before treating `id` as real. For type=user this must be prefixed 'usr:'; for type=service, 'svc:'; for type=system, the fixed literal 'system:internal'. This schema does not implement the verification itself -- see README's trust principle section.
